A Controller property named `e.{id}.{event}` binds a jQuery event handler: before `init`, Natural-TEMPLATE binds the handler to the element `#{id}` of the view (or to a `target` selector) and replaces the property with the bound element. Targets inside an [N.grid](../ui/grid.md) or [N.list](../ui/list.md) row are bound once, by delegation, and the handler receives the row index as its last argument. The template must be activated first; see [Natural-TEMPLATE conventions](conventions.md).

# Summary

| Symbol | Signature | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `e.{id}.{event}` | `"e.btnSearch.click": function (e[, ...args][, idx]) {}` | the property becomes the bound jQuery element |
| `e.{key}.{event}` object | `"e.anyKey.change": { target: selector, handler: function (e[, ...args][, idx]) {} }` | the property becomes the bound jQuery element |
| `N.template.aop.events` | `N.template.aop.events(cont, prop)` | `undefined` (internal) |

# Options

Fields of the object form:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | selector | — | Element(s) to bind, found with `N(target, cont.view)`. The `{key}` segment of the property name is then only a label. |
| `handler` | function | — | The event handler. |

# Functions

## `"e.{id}.{event}": handler`

Runs after every `p.*` component has been created, before actions and `init`.[^template][^events]

- `id` (second segment) selects `#{id}` in the view; `event` (third segment) is the jQuery event type, bound as `{event}.{pageid}` (`click.sample0001`). Segments after the third are ignored, so a jQuery namespace cannot be added in the name.
- The handler is called by jQuery: `this` is the element and the arguments are the event plus any `trigger` parameters. Rows of `N.grid` / `N.list` append the row index (see below).
- `a`, `button` and `input[type=button]` targets get `N.button` with default options (their `data-opts` apply). The button instance is not stored on the controller.
- Other targets get `cursor: pointer` when the event name contains `click`.
- When the target is a radio button or checkbox and more than one element in the view has `name="{id}"` (as generated by [N.select](../ui/select.md)), every element of that name is bound.
- Afterwards the property holds the jQuery object returned by `on()`: the bound element(s), or for rows the grid or list element. Use it to trigger the handler: `cont["e.btnSearch.click"].trigger("click")`.
- When no element matches, nothing is bound, no error is thrown, and the property keeps its declared value.
- Throws `MSG-0006` when the name has fewer than three segments or the value is neither a function nor an object.

## `"e.{key}.{event}": { target, handler }`

Same processing, but the elements are `N(target, cont.view)`: use it to bind by class, attribute or a more specific path (`"#search #eyeColor"`).[^events]

## Rows of `N.grid` and `N.list`

When the matched element lies inside a `.grid__` or `.list__` element (and not inside a `header` element), the handler is delegated from that grid or list:[^events]

```js
gridOrListElement.on(event + "." + pageid, ">.form__ " + selector, function () {
    // handler.apply(this, [...arguments, rowIndex])
});
```

- The row template (`tempRowEle`) is used for the button and cursor treatment, so rows rendered later by `bind()` or `add()` inherit it, and one handler serves every row.
- `this` is the matched element in the row. The last argument is the row index: the position of the element's row (`.closest(".form__")`) among the rendered rows (`>.form__`).
- Radio buttons, and checkboxes that form a group, are matched in rows by `[name='{id}']`.
- The property holds the grid or list element, not the target.
- The `selector` is appended after `>.form__ `, so keep it a single simple selector; a selector list (`".a, .b"`) would apply the row scope to its first part only.

## Component events

A declaration can bind any event that is triggered on the element, including custom events. [N.datepicker](../ui/datepicker.md) triggers these jQuery events on its input, in addition to calling its option handlers:[^datepicker]

| Event | Handler arguments |
|---|---|
| `onSelect` | `(e, context, selDate, monthonly)` |
| `onChangeYear` | `(e, context, year, originalEvent)` |
| `onChangeMonth` | `(e, context, month, year, originalEvent)` |
| `onBeforeShow` | `(e, context, contents)` |
| `onShow` | `(e, context, contents)` |
| `onBeforeHide` | `(e, context, contents, originalEvent)` |
| `onHide` | `(e, context)` |

Inside grid or list rows the row index follows as the last argument.

## `N.template.aop.events(cont, prop)`

Internal: binds one `e.*` property. `NT.aop.template` calls it for every property whose name starts with `e.`.[^template]

# Pitfalls

`a`, `button` and `input[type=button]` targets get `N.button`, but the property holds the bound element, not the `N.button` instance.[^events]

```js
// Wrong (legacy): cont["e.btnSave.click"].disable();
cont["e.btnSave.click"].instance("button").disable();
```

An object literal keeps only the last of two equal keys, so a controller cannot declare both forms under one name; give the second binding another key.

```js
// Wrong (legacy): "e.id.click": function (e) { ... }, "e.id.click": { target: ".div #id", handler: function (e) { ... } }
"e.id.click": function (e) { cont["p.popup.dept"].open(); },
"e.companyId.click": { target: ".div #id", handler: function (e) { cont["p.popup.company"].open(); } }
```

With a `target`, the selector is still resolved in the view; if the element is inside a grid or list, the handler is delegated from the grid or list element and the selector is matched inside each row.

jQuery runs the handlers of one element in binding order.[^form]

- Grid and list rows: the template handler is delegated from the grid or list element, so it runs after the row's own data-sync handlers (`focusout` for text inputs, `change` for `select`, `click` for radio and checkbox) and `cont["p.grid.id"].val(idx, "col")` returns the new value.
- A plain `N.form`: the template binds its handler before `init`, while the form binds its sync handlers when it binds or adds data, usually later. The template handler then runs first and the form data still holds the previous value. Read the element (`N(this).val()`), or create the form with `tpBind: true` so its handlers are placed first. A `usage: "search-box"` form calls `add()` before the events are bound, so its sync handlers come first unless a later `unbind()` (for example through `autoUnbind`) re-attaches them.

Handlers written as arrow functions have no element `this`; use `e.currentTarget` (or `function`) when you need it. The controller is still reachable through the `cont` variable.

A declaration whose element is missing is skipped silently, and `cont["e.x.click"].trigger(...)` then fails because the property is still a function.

# Examples

Button, delegated row events and a datepicker event:

```js
const cont = N(".sample0004").cont({
    "p.form.search": { usage: "search-box" },
    "p.datepicker.searchDate": {},
    "p.grid.master": { height: 300, action: "bind" },

    "e.btnSearch.click": function (e) {
        e.preventDefault();
        cont["c.getList"]().submit(function (data) {
            cont["p.grid.master"].bind(data);
        });
    },

    "e.btnDetail.click": function (e, idx) {            // #btnDetail is in the grid's row template
        e.preventDefault();
        N.log(cont["p.grid.master"].data()[idx]);
    },

    "e.qty.focusout": function (e, idx) {               // row inputs: the grid row is synced first
        N.log(cont["p.grid.master"].val(idx, "qty"));
    },

    "e.searchDate.onSelect": function (e, context, selDate, monthonly) {
        N.log(selDate.obj.formatDate(selDate.format));
    },

    "e.eyeColor.change": {
        target: "#search #eyeColor",
        handler: function (e) {
            cont["e.btnSearch.click"].trigger("click");
        }
    },

    "c.getList": () => cont["p.form.search"].data(false).comm("sample/getList.json"),

    init: function (view, request) {
        cont["e.btnSearch.click"].trigger("click");
    }
});
```
